info.name: Project Task Management API
info.description:
Complete Postman collection for the Project Task Management System built with Hono + TypeScript + PostgreSQL.

---

## Setup
1. Import this collection into Postman.
2. Set the `base_url` variable to your server URL (default: http://localhost:3000).
3. Run **Register** or **Login** first — the access token is saved automatically.
4. All protected routes use the `{{access_token}}` variable automatically.

## Roles
- **superadmin** — Platform owner. No org. Sees everything.
- **admin** — Company manager. Scoped to one org.
- **developer** — Team member. Sees only assigned projects/tasks.

request.description: Check if the server is running.

item.name: Auth
item.description: Authentication endpoints — register, login, OTP, token refresh, and logout. No auth header needed except logout.

request.description:
Create a new user account.

**role** can be: `superadmin`, `admin`, `developer`

Returns access token + refresh token. Token is saved automatically to collection variables.

**No auth required.**

Login with email and password.

Returns access token + refresh token. Tokens are saved automatically to collection variables.

**No auth required.**

Possible errors:
- 401 Invalid credentials
- 403 Account is inactive
- 401 Account uses OTP login (no password set)

response.name: 403 Inactive Account

request.description:
Request a 6-digit OTP sent to the given email address.

OTP expires in **5 minutes**.

The email must belong to a registered (non-deleted) user.

**No auth required.**

response.name: 200 OK

request.description:
Submit the 6-digit OTP received by email to login.

OTP must be exactly 6 digits. On success, tokens are returned and saved automatically.

**No auth required.**

response.name: 400 OTP Expired

request.description:
Get a new access token using the refresh token.

The old refresh token is **deleted** and a new one is issued (token rotation). New tokens are saved automatically.

**No auth required.**

Logout and invalidate the current session.

The refresh token is deleted from the database, making it unusable.

**Auth required** — Bearer token in header.

item.name: Users
item.description:
User management — list users, view profile, update own profile, and toggle user status.

All routes require a valid Bearer token.

query.description: Filter by role: superadmin | admin | developer
Field to sort by (e.g. createdAt, name)

request.description:
Get a paginated list of users.

- **Superadmin**: sees all users across all orgs
- **Admin**: sees users in their own org only
- **Developer**: sees users in their own org only

Supports filtering, sorting, and pagination.

Get details of a specific user by their UUID.

- **Superadmin**: can view any user
- **Admin / Developer**: can only view users within their own org

Update your own profile information.

All fields are optional — send only what you want to update.

Updatable fields: `name`, `phone`, `avatarUrl`

**Any role** can use this.

Activate or deactivate a user account.

**status** must be: `active` or `inactive`

- **Superadmin**: can update any user
- **Admin**: can update users within their own org only
- **Developer**: not allowed (403)

An inactive user cannot log in.

item.name: Organizations
item.description:
Organization management.

- Create orgs and assign admins → Superadmin only
- Add/register developers → Admin only
- Remove members → Superadmin or Admin (own org)

All routes require a valid Bearer token.

request.description:
Create a new organization.

**Superadmin only.**

- `name`: Organization display name (min 2 chars)
- `slug`: Unique URL-friendly identifier — lowercase letters, numbers, and hyphens only (e.g. `my-org-123`)

Slug must be globally unique.

Org ID is saved automatically to `{{org_id}}`.

response.name: 409 Slug Conflict

request.description:
Get a list of all organizations on the platform.

**Superadmin only.**

Returns all orgs with their member counts.

Get details of a specific organization including all its members.

- **Superadmin**: can view any org
- **Admin**: can only view their own org
- **Developer**: not allowed (403)

Assign an existing user (with admin role) to an organization.

**Superadmin only.**

The user must already exist in the system and must not already be assigned to another organization. An admin can only belong to one org.

response.name: 409 Already Assigned

request.description:
Create a new user account with `admin` role and immediately assign them to the specified organization.

**Superadmin only.**

This is the recommended way to add a new admin — creates the account and assigns to org in one step.

Add an existing user (developer role) to the admin's organization.

**Admin only** — and only to their own org.

The admin's orgId is used automatically. The `orgId` in the URL must match the admin's own org.

Create a new user account with `developer` role and immediately assign them to the admin's organization.

**Admin only.**

This is the recommended way to add a new developer to your team.

Remove a member from an organization.

- **Superadmin**: can remove from any org
- **Admin**: can remove from their own org only
- **Developer**: not allowed (403)

This removes the membership record. The user account itself is NOT deleted.

response.name: 404 Not Found

item.name: Projects
item.description:
Project management — create, list, update, and soft-delete projects.

- Create/Update/Delete → Admin or Superadmin only
- List/View → all roles (scoped: developers see assigned projects only)

All routes require a valid Bearer token.

query.description: Filter by status: active | on_hold | completed
Field to sort by (e.g. createdAt, title)

request.description:
Get a paginated list of projects.

- **Superadmin**: sees all projects across all orgs
- **Admin**: sees all projects in their org
- **Developer**: sees only projects they are assigned to

Supports filtering by title, status, creator. Sorting and pagination supported.

response.name: 200 OK

request.description:
Get full details of a project including its assigned members.

- **Superadmin**: can view any project
- **Admin**: can view projects in their org
- **Developer**: can only view projects they are assigned to

response.name: 200 OK

request.description:
Create a new project in the admin's organization.

**Admin or Superadmin only.**

- `title`: required
- `description`: optional
- `logoUrl`: optional, URL to project logo image
- `assignedUserIds`: optional array of developer user IDs to assign to this project

Project starts with status `active`.

Project ID is saved automatically to `{{project_id}}`.

response.name: 201 Created

request.description:
Update a project's details.

**Admin or Superadmin only.**

All fields are optional — send only what you want to update.

- `status` options: `active`, `on_hold`, `completed`
- `assignedUserIds`: **replaces** the full member list (not additive)

**Note**: When `assignedUserIds` is provided, all existing members are removed and replaced with the new list.

Soft-delete a project. The project is NOT permanently removed — `deletedAt` is set.

**Admin or Superadmin only.**

**Important**: This will fail with `400` if the project has any tasks that are not `completed`. All tasks must be completed before a project can be archived.

response.name: 400 Pending Tasks Exist

item.name: Tasks
item.description:
Task management — create, list, update, and soft-delete tasks.

- Create/Delete → Admin or Superadmin only
- Update → Admin (all fields), Developer (status only — on assigned tasks)
- List/View → all roles (scoped: developers see assigned tasks only)

All routes require a valid Bearer token.

query.description: Filter: to_do | in_progress | on_hold | overdue | completed
Search in task title and description
Field to sort by (e.g. createdAt, dueDate, priority)

request.description:
Get a paginated list of tasks.

- **Superadmin**: sees all tasks across all orgs
- **Admin**: sees all tasks in their org
- **Developer**: sees only tasks assigned to them

Supports filtering by status, priority, project, assigned developer, and text search. Sorting and pagination supported.

response.name: 200 OK

request.description:
Get full details of a task including all assignees.

- **Superadmin**: can view any task
- **Admin**: can view tasks in their org
- **Developer**: can only view tasks assigned to them

response.name: 200 OK

body.raw:
{
  "title": "Build login page",
  "description": "Implement the login UI with email and password",
  "priority": "high",
  "dueDate": "2024-02-01",
  "projectId": "{{project_id}}",
  "assignedUserIds": []
}

request.description:
Create a new task inside a project.

**Admin or Superadmin only.**

- `title`: required
- `projectId`: required — must be a valid project UUID
- `description`: optional
- `priority`: optional — `low`, `medium` (default), `high`, `urgent`
- `dueDate`: optional — format `YYYY-MM-DD`
- `assignedUserIds`: optional array of developer UUIDs to assign

Task starts with status `to_do`.

Task ID is saved automatically to `{{task_id}}`.

Update a task's full details.

**Admin**: can update all fields.
**Developer**: can ONLY update `status` (see the Developer version below).

All fields are optional — send only what you want to update.

- `status` options: `to_do`, `in_progress`, `on_hold`, `overdue`, `completed`
- `priority` options: `low`, `medium`, `high`, `urgent`
- `assignedUserIds`: **replaces** the full assignee list

Update only the status of a task.

**Developer role**: can ONLY send `status` — sending any other field returns 403.

Developer must be assigned to this task.

**status** options: `to_do`, `in_progress`, `on_hold`, `overdue`, `completed`

When a developer marks a task as `completed` and all other tasks in the project are also `completed`, the project status will automatically update to `completed`.

Soft-delete a task. The task is NOT permanently removed — `deletedAt` is set.

**Admin or Superadmin only.**

**Important**: A task can only be deleted if its status is `completed`. Deleting an in-progress or to-do task returns 400.

response.name: 400 Task Not Completed

item.name: Uploads
item.description:
File upload support via pre-signed S3/Backblaze B2 URLs.

The server does NOT store files directly. Instead it returns a pre-signed URL that the client uses to upload directly to cloud storage.

All routes require a valid Bearer token.

request.description:
Generate a pre-signed URL to upload a file directly to S3/Backblaze B2.

**Any authenticated user** can request an upload URL.

- `fileName`: required — name of the file (e.g. `photo.jpg`)
- `contentType`: required — MIME type (e.g. `image/jpeg`, `image/png`, `application/pdf`)
- `folder`: optional — upload destination folder: `avatars`, `logos`, or `attachments`

**How to use the response:**
1. Get the `uploadUrl` from the response
2. Make a `PUT` request to that URL with the file as the raw body and the correct `Content-Type` header
3. After upload, use the `fileUrl` as the stored file URL (e.g. save to `avatarUrl` on user profile)

Pre-signed URL expires in **10 minutes**.
